info.title: TeamDynamix Web API
info.description:
The TeamDynamix Web API provides a series of RESTful web services to facilitate integration with various areas of the TeamDynamix solution.

It is important to note that these web services have been designed to send and receive data in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) format. Other formats, such as XML or plain text, are not supported. When calling the web API, this requires a content type of application/json.

Authentication is based on JWT (JSON Web Token) Bearer tokens included in the Authorization header of HTTP requests. Tokens can be obtained through standard authentication methods and are valid for 24 hours. Where noted, some actions require the use of a special key-based administrative account. For these actions, tokens obtained through the standard login methods will not work.

get.summary: Gets the custom attributes for the specified component.
get.description:
Authorization RequiredThis endpoint requires authentication.
Rate Limit60 request(s) per 20 second(s) per IP address. Additional rate limits may apply based on system configuration.

parameters.name: componentId
parameters.description:
The component ID.

| Name | Value | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| Project | 1 | Indicates that custom attributes are for projects and project requests in the Projects and Portfolio Planning systems. |
| Issue | 3 | Indicates that custom attributes are for issues in the Projects system. |
| File Cabinet File | 8 | Indicates that custom attributes are for files in the File Cabinet system. |
| Ticket | 9 | Indicates that custom attributes are for tickets in the Tickets system. |
| Account | 14 | Indicates that custom attributes are for accounts. |
| Knowledge Base Article | 26 | Indicates that custom attributes are for articles in the Knowledge Base system. |
| Asset | 27 | Indicates that custom attributes are for assets in the Assets/CIs system. |
| Vendor | 28 | Indicates that custom attributes are for vendors in the Assets/CIs system. |
| Contract | 29 | Indicates that custom attributes are for contracts in the Assets/CIs system. |
| Product Model | 30 | Indicates that custom attributes are for product models in the Assets/CIs system. |
| Person | 31 | Indicates that custom attributes are for people. |
| Service | 47 | Indicates that custom attributes are for services. |
| Configuration Item | 63 | Indicates that custom attributes are for standalone configuration items in the Assets/CIs system. |
| Location | 71 | Indicates that custom attributes are for locations. |
| Risk | 72 | Indicates that custom attributes are for Risk Register risks in the Projects and Portfolio Planning systems. |
| Location Room | 80 | Indicates that custom attributes are for rooms associated with a location. |
| Service Offering | 87 | Indicates that custom attributes are for service offerings. |
| Consumable | 98 | Indicates that custom attributes are for consumables in the Assets/CIs system. |

parameters.name: associatedTypeId
parameters.description: The associated project type ID to get attributes for.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description:
The associated platform application ID to filter attributes.
For Ticket attributes (componentId=9): - Omitted or null — all ticket attributes across all applications, including all global ticket attributes. - 0 — only global ticket attributes. - Greater than 0 — attributes for the specified application plus global ticket attributes.
For all other components, omitting or passing 0 returns all attributes; a specific ID filters to that application.

200.description: Returns the active custom attributes for the component. Protected and/or inactive custom attributes will be excluded. For Ticket attributes, global attributes are indicated by an AppID of 0.

post.summary: Accepts a file, stores that file on disk, and places an entry into the database to indicate to the import file processor to pick up the file and run a People Import on it.
post.description:
Requirements:

  • The file must be in .xlsx format
  • The file must have a header row with supported TeamDynamix fields as column names. Download the template file using the instructions below for more details.

This process can be used to:

  • Update existing customer and user records
  • Create new customer records if no existing customer is found and the user type is Customer
  • Create new users if no existing user is found and the user type is User

This process will not:

  • Convert existing Customer records to User records or vice-versa

Updating Existing Records:

The following matching logic is used to determine if a records should be udpated or created.

  1. Username - If there already exists one or more people, regardless of active status, with the same TeamDynamix username as a row that is being imported, those records will be updated from the spreadsheet. This field will only be used for the purposes of matching. TeamDynamix username fields will not be updated as part of this process.
  2. Authentication Username - If there already exists one or more people, regardless of active status, with the same TeamDynamix authentication username as a row that is being imported, those records will be updated from the spreadsheet. This is the Auth Username specified for the user in the TDAdmin application. This field will only be used for the purposes of matching. TeamDynamix authentication username fields will not be updated as part of this process.
  3. Organizational ID - If there already exists one or more people, regardless of active status, with the same organizational ID as a row that is being imported, those records will be updated from the spreadsheet.
  4. Primary Email Address - If there already exists one or more people, regardless of active status, with the same primary email as a row that is being imported, those records will be updated from the spreadsheet.

User organizational IDs and primary email addresses will be updated as part of this process as long as they are not the fields which records are matched on.

Creating New Records:

When creating records, the default is to create a Customer. If you do not include the User Type column and specify a user type of User, Customer records will be created.

Not Mapping Values vs. Clearing Values :

It is important to note that this process will only attempt to modify values for fields which are included in the import sheet and can be mapped to a TeamDynamix field. For instance, if you do not provide a column for a user's home phone, that value will not be mapped and thus will not be changed in any way. If you want to clear values, be sure that you provide a column for the field you want to clear and leave the cell values blank.

Schedule:

Calls to this endpoint are not processed in real-time. All import jobs are run in a batch process overnight.

Download the Template File:

See this TeamDynamix Knowledge Base article for a template upload file with the supported columns. The template will contain all necessary instructions for how to obtain column values for each column.

Accepts File UploadsThis endpoint accepts file uploads as part of the form data.

Applications is a full replace: standard applications omitted from the request are removed, an empty collection removes them all, and omitting the property entirely leaves standard applications unchanged. OrgApplications is a full replace: organizationally defined applications omitted from the request are removed, an empty collection removes them all, and omitting the property entirely leaves them unchanged. An organizationally defined application paired with an invalid security role ID is also removed. External apps aren't associated with security roles, so a security role ID paired with an external app ID is ignored. Application Access Usage Examples:
  • Standard Applications:
    1. Changes application access to only TDNext and MyWork:
      "Applications": ["TDNext","MyWork"]
    2. Clears all application access:
      "Applications": []
    3. Makes no change to application access at all:
      "Applications": null
  • Organizationally-Defined Applications:
    1. Changes application access to only Ticket app 1 and Client Portal app 2:
      "OrgApplications": [{"id":1,"securityroleid":"role1here"},{"id":2,"securityroleid":"role2here"}]
    2. Clears all application access:
      "OrgApplications": []
    3. Makes no change to application access at all:

patch.description:
This only patches the person itself, custom attributes, applications, and organization applications — other collections on the person aren't supported. You can't change the person's password, organization, or user type through this method. Applications is a full replace by default, or append mode when appendApplications=true: in replace mode, standard applications omitted from the request are removed; in append mode, only the provided applications are added and omitted ones stay. An empty collection removes all standard applications in replace mode and is a no-op in append mode. Omitting the property makes no change either way. OrgApplications is a full replace by default, or append mode when appendApplications=true: in replace mode, organizationally defined applications omitted from the request are removed; in append mode, only the provided applications are added and omitted ones stay. An empty collection removes all organizationally defined applications in replace mode and is a no-op in append mode. Omitting the property makes no change either way. In append mode, an organizationally defined application the person already has access to is left unchanged — its security role and administrator flag are not updated even if new values are supplied for it. Use replace mode to change the role or administrator flag on an existing org application. In replace mode, an org application paired with an invalid security role ID is also removed. External apps aren't associated with security roles, so a security role ID paired with an external app ID is ignored. Application Access Usage Examples:
  • Standard Applications:
    1. Changes application access to only TDNext and MyWork:
      {"op": "add", "path": "/applications", "value": ["TDNext","MyWork"]}
    2. Clears all application access:
      {"op": "add", "path": "/applications", "value": []}
    3. Makes no change to application access at all:
      {"op": "add", "path": "/applications", "value": null}
  • Organizationally Defined Applications:
    1. Changes application access to only Ticket app 1 and Client Portal app 2:
      {"op": "add", "path": "/orgapplications", "value": [{"id":1,"securityroleid":"role1here"},{"id":2,"securityroleid":"role2here"}]}
    2. Clears all application access:
      {"op": "add", "path": "/orgapplications", "value": []}
    3. Makes no change to application access at all:
      {"op": "add", "path": "/orgapplications", "value": null}

post.summary: Adds or edits one or more time entries.
post.description:
Time entries will be created if their ID is zero or negative and edited if they have a positive ID. You cannot add or edit more than 50 items at once. If you need to work with a larger set of records, you will need to perform multiple calls.

A collection of successes and failures will be returned. Successes will be accompanied by the IDs of the new time entries. Failures will be accompanied by an error code and error message. Because some operations may complete successfully while others fail, it is important for the caller to inspect the results of the failures collection.

In order to add or edit time for a user, they must be in your organization and be a standard User.

Time entries cannot be added or edited for reports that are submitted or approved or on days marked as locked days within your organization.

Time entries using limited time accounts cannot be negative, must have a limit defined for the user for the time period you're working with, and the number of hours in this limit cannot be exceeded.

Once a time entry has been created, you cannot change many properties about it, including the item it is associated with and the person who entered time. If you need to do these things, we recommend deleting the entry and re-adding it using the corrected values.

This endpoint can be used to delete time entries by setting their minutes to zero. However, time can only be deleted when authenticated as an Admin Service Account or as the user who the time is for.

Add or edit operations are allowed either as the user the time is for or as an Admin Service Account. An exception to this rule is if you are working with task time, have the Projects application, are on the project in question, and have permission to add time for other users. An additional exception is when working with ticket or ticket task time and you have the application permission to add time for others within the ticketing application in question.

Time entry will only be allowed for time accounts available on the item you're trying to enter time for. Additionally, the user in question must be able to access the item that the time is for which can depend on applications and permissions granted to users as well as project / workspace / request / ticketing application membership.

The user you are entering time for must be active and have the time and expenses application.

Authorization RequiredThis endpoint requires authentication.
Permission RequiredTDTimeExpense
Rate Limit60 request(s) per 60 second(s) per IP address. Additional rate limits may apply based on system configuration.

200.description: Returns an object indicating which operations succeeded and failed as well as any error messages for failures and IDs for new additions.

You cannot delete time entries associated with time reports that have been submitted or approved.

You can only delete up to 50 entries per call. If you need to delete more than that, you will need to make multiple calls to the API.

parameters.description: Whether to reassign the removed member's in-flight work (DelegateMaterials, the default) or delete the items they created (DeleteMaterials). | Name | Value | Description | |------|-------|-------------| | Delegate Materials | 0 | The removed member's work (files, schedules, etc.) is reassigned to the delegate. | | Delete Materials | 1 | The removed member's created items are deleted; any remaining file/revision ownership is still reassigned to the delegate. |

parameters.description: The number of configuration items to return per page. Must be greater than 0 and no more than 250. Defaults to 50.

parameters.description: The 1-based page number to retrieve. Must be no more than 2147483647 divided by pageSize. Defaults to 1.

requestBody.description: The searching parameters to use. Identical to the body accepted by POST /api/{appId}/cmdb/search; MaxResults is ignored when paging.

200.description: Returns a page of configuration items matching the specified criteria.

put.summary: Edits the specified category.
put.description:
This will not update the category's permission options (such as that of permission inheritance, public status, or whitelist/blacklist options).

When the request body is JSON, only the properties it includes are updated. Any property that is omitted keeps its current value, so a category keeps its parent unless a parent ID is supplied. Supply a parent ID of 0 to move the category to the root. A request body in any other format replaces the whole category, as before.

In a JSON body, a number or yes/no property (the parent ID or order) given an explicit null, an empty string or any other value that cannot be converted leaves it unchanged. A null description clears it, and a null name is rejected. A JSON body that cannot be read is rejected with a 400 and nothing is saved.

When the parent changes, a category whose stored settings inherit permissions re-inherits them from its new parent, as it does in the admin UI. The permission values in the request body (public status, whitelist and permission inheritance) are ignored.

post.summary: Creates a project.
post.description:
This endpoint emulates the project creation process in TDNext with a few notable exceptions:

  1. The project manager and alternate managers may be explicitly set differently from the calling user.
  2. No resource requests will be generated for project or alternate managers.
  3. Project/alternate manager employee status and capacity date requirements will be ignored.
  4. Adding a project to a portfolio or program is not supported.

The following requirements must be met by the caller to create a project:

  1. The caller must have TDNext access, as well as full TDProjects access.
  2. The caller must have the global security role permission to Add Projects.

The specified new project manager/alternate managers must meet the following requirements:

  1. Be an active user of type User (neither service accounts nor resource placeholders of any kind can be project managers).
  2. Have access to both the TDNext and TDProjects applications (access to view projects in a Client Portal is insufficient).
  3. Have a primary functional role.
Authorization RequiredThis endpoint requires authentication.
Permission RequiredTDProjects
Rate Limit60 request(s) per 60 second(s) per IP address. Additional rate limits may apply based on system configuration.

post.summary: Closes a project.
post.description:
Closing a project is more than a status change — it also handles outstanding tasks, issues, and risks, cancels pending resource requests, truncates schedules, and optionally sends a closure survey. The following requirements must be met:

  1. The caller must have TDNext access and Analysis or Projects access.
  2. The caller must be an admin service account, the project manager, or an alternate manager.
  3. StatusID must refer to an active closure-type project status for the project's application.
  4. When CloseIssues is true, NewIssueStatusID must be an active issue status for the project's application with a Completed or Cancelled status class.
  5. When CloseRisks is true, NewRiskStatusID must be an active risk status for the project's application with a Completed or Cancelled status class.
Authorization RequiredThis endpoint requires authentication.
Permission RequiredTDAnalysis,TDProjects
Rate Limit60 request(s) per 60 second(s) per IP address. Additional rate limits may apply based on system configuration.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The project ID.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Optional project application ID to scope the lookup. If null or 0, the default project application is used. Use 0 for no specific application context.

requestBody.description: The close request parameters.

200.description: Returns the updated project after closure.

post.description:
When posting a plain comment, Body is required. A blank body is rejected with a 400 Bad Request response. For a rich-text body (IsRichHtml), markup that has no visible text and no image once sanitized for storage counts as blank (for example

 

, or a video/iframe embed, which is not kept in feed entries). If the comment cannot be added, a 400 Bad Request response is returned instead of the entry. When posting a status update, the caller must be the project manager, an alternate manager, or a user with the Analysis – Can Update All Projects Status permission. The effective health and status after the call must be consistent: on-hold statuses require OnHold health, and non-on-hold statuses require a non-on-hold health value. Omitted fields default to the project's current values for this consistency check.
Authorization RequiredThis endpoint requires authentication.
Permission RequiredTDAnalysis,TDProjects

Each newly assigned manager (primary or alternate) must be an active account of type User with a primary functional role and access to this project's application — managers already in their role are not re-validated. New managers and alternate managers are notified by default.

post.summary: Adds a project's direct portfolio associations.
post.description:
Portfolios the project is already directly assigned to are left unchanged. An unresolvable portfolio ID is rejected with a validation error, and none of the requested portfolios are added if any ID can't be resolved. The caller must be the project manager, an alternate manager, a portfolio/program manager with permission to manage projects in their portfolios/programs, a user with the Manage All Projects permission, a user with the Edit All Portfolios and Programs permission, or an admin service account. A project cannot end up associated with the same portfolio through more than one path — e.g. directly assigned to a portfolio while also belonging to a program under that same portfolio. Such conflicts are rejected with a clear validation error instead of applying a partial change.

post.summary: Adds a resource to a project.
post.description:
This endpoint emulates the behavior to add resources to projects as seen in TDNext with a few notable exceptions:

  1. No schedules will be set via this endpoint.
  2. Resource requests will not be generated even if they normally would in the UI.
  3. Resource employee status and capacity date requirements will be ignored.

The following requirements must be met by the caller to add resources to a project:

  1. The project must be open (though active is not a requirement).
  2. The project cannot be the private team or a template project.
  3. The caller must have TDNext access, as well as Analysis or Projects access.
  4. The caller must be an admin service account, the project manager, an alternate manager, or a program/portfolio manager with permissions to manage projects in their program/portfolio.

The specified resource to add to the project must meet the following requirements:

  1. Be an active user of type User or Resource Placeholder
  2. Have access to TDNext and Projects, or have Client Portal View Projects permissions in at least one Client Portal.
  3. Have a primary functional role.
  4. Not be on the project already.
Authorization RequiredThis endpoint requires authentication.
Permission RequiredTDAnalysis,TDProjects
Rate Limit60 request(s) per 60 second(s) per IP address. Additional rate limits may apply based on system configuration.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The project ID.

parameters.name: resourceUid
parameters.description: The UID of the resource to add.

parameters.name: notifyManagers
parameters.description: Whether or not to notify the project manager, alternate managers and any relevant resource pool managers about the new project resource.

parameters.name: notifyResource
parameters.description: Whether or not to notify the project resource that they have been added to the project.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: The application ID to use as context. Use 0 for no specific application context.

200.description: Returns the full project user information for the newly added resource if successful.

post.summary: Reorders the lists (columns) on a cardwall board.
post.description:
The archive list (ID 0), if included in sortedListIds, is ignored and never reordered. Every other list on the board must be included exactly once - a partial list, a duplicate ID, or an ID that isn't found on this board is rejected. The remaining lists are assigned a zero-based, contiguous Order matching their relative position in the supplied array (the archive list, if present, does not consume a position).

The calling user must satisfy the following requirements to reorder board lists:
  1. Have access to both the TDNext and TDProjects applications.
  2. The specified project must be open and active (not closed).
  3. The caller must have read access to the board and be a project manager.
Authorization RequiredThis endpoint requires authentication.
Permission RequiredTDProjects
Rate Limit60 request(s) per 60 second(s) per IP address. Additional rate limits may apply based on system configuration.

put.description:

If Limits contains an entry, only the first one is saved — a board list supports at most one work-in-progress limit. If Limits is omitted or empty, any existing limit on the list is removed.

The calling user must satisfy the following requirements to edit board lists:
  1. Have access to both the TDNext and TDProjects applications.
  2. The specified project must be open and active (not closed).
  3. The caller must have read access to the board and be a project manager.
  4. The list being edited cannot be the board's archive list (ID 0).

This operation requires the permission to modify service categories.

This will not update the category's permission options (such as that of permission inheritance, public status, or allowlist/denylist options).

When the request body is JSON, only the properties it includes are updated. Any property that is omitted keeps its current value, so a category keeps its parent unless a parent ID is supplied. Supply a parent ID of 0 to move the category to the root. A request body in any other format replaces the whole category, as before.

In a JSON body, a number or yes/no property (the parent ID, order, active status or icon code) given an explicit null, an empty string or any other value that cannot be converted leaves it unchanged. A null description clears it, and a null name is rejected. A JSON body that cannot be read is rejected with a 400 and nothing is saved.

When the parent changes, a category whose stored settings inherit permissions re-inherits them from its new parent, as it does in the admin UI. Any permission inheritance value in the request body is ignored.

Remarks: Since configuration items support custom forms, the IsRequired property is ignored. Alternatively, required status is driven by the form, which can be changed via the FormID property.

BackingItemID.description: The ID of the underlying TeamDynamix item in the system that this configuration item represents. Remarks: In the case of system-maintained configuration items, this will have the ID of the underlying item, such as an asset or service ID, that this configuration item represents. The specific type of underlying item can be identified using the BackingItemType property. In the case of configuration items that are not system-maintained, this will be functionally equivalent to the ID.

Remarks: In the case of system-maintained configuration items, this will have the type of the underlying item, such as Asset or Service. Remarks: Assets and Service Catalog services are two examples of system-maintained configuration items, as they are backed by those appropriate systems but still have alternate representations as configuration items. Describes the different types of conflicts that can be detected for
a scheduled maintenance activity for a CI.

| Name | Value | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| None | 0 | Indicates that no conflicts were detected. |
| Outside Maintenance Window | 1 | Indicates that an activity takes place outside of the CI's maintenance window. |
| During Blackout Window | 2 | Indicates that an activity takes place during a blackout window. |
| Conflicts with Existing Activity | 4 | Indicates that an activity conflicts with a pre-existing activity scheduled for the CI. |
| Outside Child CI's Maintenance Window | 8 | Indicates that an activity takes place outside the maintenance window of one or more of the CI's operational children. |
| Conflicts with Child CI's Existing Activity | 16 | Indicates that an activity conflicts with a pre-existing activity on one of the CI's operational children. |
| Conflicts with Parent CI's Existing Activity | 32 | Indicates that an activity conflicts with a pre-existing activity on one of the CI's operational parents. |

ConsumableQuantityAdjustment.description:
A request to change the inventory quantity of a consumable at a particular location/room pair by a signed amount.

The Adjustment is added to the pair's current quantity, or becomes its initial quantity when the pair has no inventory yet, so concurrent adjustments from multiple callers both count instead of overwriting one another.

Adjustment.description:
The amount to change the location/room pair's quantity by. Positive values add stock and negative values remove it. When the pair has no inventory yet, this becomes its initial quantity. A value of 0 leaves the pair unchanged.

Remarks: Inventory is allowed to go negative (a ticket may draw more than is in stock), so a negative result is not rejected.

LocationID.description: The ID of the location for the inventory being adjusted. Value: The ID of the location for the inventory being adjusted, or 0 for the "Unassigned" pseudo-location.

LocationRoomID.description: The ID of the location room for the inventory being adjusted. Value: The ID of the location room for the inventory being adjusted, or 0 when the inventory is not associated with a specific room (including the "Unassigned" pseudo-location).

The required status of the attribute. Value: true if the attribute is required; otherwise, false.

Remarks: When attributes are used in conjunction with a system that is entirely based on custom forms (such as tickets, assets, or configuration items), this property has no relevance as required status is instead derived from the form.

IsUpdatable.description: The updatable status of the attribute. Value: true if the attribute can be modified through "Update" views, as opposed to a full "Edit" view; otherwise, false.

Name.description: The name of the attribute.

Order.description:
The explicit sort order of the attribute.

Remarks: Attributes are first sorted by order (ascending) and their name (also ascending). In addition, if attribute sections are supported, attributes will be grouped by section.

SectionID.description: The ID of the section associated with the attribute.

SectionName.description: The name of the section associated with the attribute. Read-only.

Value.description:
The current value of the attribute. Read-only on attribute definition endpoints.

Remarks: 

For choice attributes, this will be a comma-separated list of the selected choice IDs.

For person-type custom attributes, this will be the GUID of the selected person.

For location-type custom attributes, this will be the ID of the selected location.

For location and room-type custom attributes, this will be the ID of the selected room.

ValueText.description: The current value of the attribute, as a read-only text format. Value: A human-readable text version of the current Value of the attribute. Remarks: For choice attributes, this will be a comma-separated list of the selected choice names. For person-type custom attributes, this will be the name of the selected person. For location-type custom attributes, this will be the name of the selected location. For location and room-type custom attributes, this will be the names of both the selected location and the selected room, separated by a hyphen.

CustomAttributeChoice.description: A single choice for a custom attribute.

DateCreated.description: The created date of the attribute choice.

DateModified.description: The last modified date of the attribute choice.

ID.description: The ID of the attribute choice.

Remarks: Inactive choices can still be used in searching and reporting, but should not be used for new items going forward.

display text for the choice.

Order.description:
The order of the attribute choice in the list.

Remarks: Choices are first sorted by order (ascending) and their name (also ascending).

Delegation.description:
Represents a delegated approval window, in which one user (the delegate) may act on approvals on behalf of another user (the primary approver) for a set date range.

Create with POST; edit with PUT .../{id}, where the ID is supplied in the route. Past delegations cannot be edited.

DelegatedFromFullName.description: The full name of the primary approver being delegated from. Read-only.

DelegatedFromUID.description: The UID of the primary approver being delegated from.

DelegatedToFullName.description: The full name of the delegate being delegated to. Read-only.

DelegatedToUID.description:
The UID of the delegate being delegated to. Must be a different user than
DelegatedFromUID.

EndDate.description: The date the delegation window ends (inclusive). Cannot be before the start date.

ID.description:
The unique ID of the delegation. Server-assigned and read-only; when editing, supply the ID
in the route rather than the body.

NotifyDelegate.description: Whether to send a notification to the delegate when the delegation is saved. Defaults to false.

StartDate.description: The date the delegation window starts (inclusive). Cannot be in the past.

Status.description: The computed status of the delegation window.

DelegationSearch.description: A set of filtering options used for searching delegated approval windows.

DelegatedFromUID.description: The UID of the primary approver (delegated from) to filter on.

DelegatedToUID.description: The UID of the delegate (delegated to) to filter on.

EndDateTo.description: The upper bound for the window end date. Only windows ending on or before this date are returned.

MaxResults.description: The maximum number of results to return. If not provided, all matching results are returned.

StartDateFrom.description: The lower bound for the window start date. Only windows starting on or after this date are returned.

Status.description: The computed status to filter on. If not provided, all statuses are returned.

DelegationStatus.description:
Describes the status of a delegated approval window, computed from its date range.

| Name | Value | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| Past | 0 | The delegation window has ended. |
| Present | 1 | The delegation window is currently active. |
| Future | 2 | The delegation window has not yet started. |
| Cancelled | 3 | The delegation was cancelled during its active window. |
x-enumDescriptions: The delegation window has ended.
The delegation window is currently active.
The delegation window has not yet started.
The delegation was cancelled during its active window.

IsParent.description: Indicates if the feed entry is a parent of other feed entries. Value: true if the feed entry is a parent of other feed entries; otherwise,false. Remarks: A feed entry can be a parent when a bulk or cascading operation is performed. For example, when a ticket update is cascaded to its children, a feed entry is created on every affected ticket. The originating update is marked as a parent and all other updates are children of that parent update. Similarly, a "Multiple" update will act as a parent for the feed entries created as a result of bulk-updating, bulk-commenting, or bulk-importing tickets, assets, and/or configuration items. When viewing application-wide feeds, only feed entries that lack a parent will be included. However, when viewing item-level feeds, all feed entries that reference that item will be included.

LicenseTypes.description:
Describes the different types of licenses that are used
to configure security roles
and audit license compliance.

| Name | Value | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| None | 0 | Identifies an unknown license type. |
| Enterprise | 1 | Identifies an Enterprise license type. |
| Project Manager | 2 | Identifies a Project Manager license type. |
| Technician | 3 | Identifies a Technician license type. |
| Team Member | 4 | Identifies a Team Member license type. |
| Student Technician | 5 | Identifies a Student Technician license type. |
| Client | 6 | Identifies a Client license type. |
| Client + Reporting | 7 | Identifies a Client + Reporting license type. |
| Project Manager + Reporting | 8 | Identifies a Project Manager + Reporting license type. |
| Technician + Reporting | 9 | Identifies a Technician + Reporting license type. |
| Team Member + Reporting | 10 | Identifies a Team Member + Reporting license type. |

The total value of the consumable item held here: quantity multiplied by unit cost. A
negative quantity is treated as zero, so this is never negative.

UnitCost.description:
The consumable item's unit cost as it stands today, not a snapshot taken when the
association was created.

Floor.description: The floor information associated with the location room.

ModifiedDate.description: The last modified date of the maintenance activity.

ModifiedFullName.description: The full name of the user who last modified the maintenance activity.

ModifiedUid.description: The UID of the user who last modified the maintenance activity.

NotifyResponsible.description: Whether to notify the responsible party. Always true; any value sent is ignored. Value: true if it should notify; otherwise, false.

Order.description:

PercentComplete.description: The percent complete of the maintenance activity. To change it, post a feed entry to the maintenance activity.

ResponsibleEmail.description:

ResponsibleFullName.description:
The full name of the user responsible for the maintenance activity.

ResponsibleGroupID.description: The ID of the group responsible for the maintenance activity.

ResponsibleGroupName.description:

maintenance windows.

MoveTicketOptions.description: The options for moving a ticket to a different ticketing application.

Comments.description: The comments of the move (ticket) to application feed entry.

IsRichHtml.description: Indicates if the comment is rich-text or plain-text. Value: true if the comment is rich-text; otherwise, false.

The ID of the form in the destination ticketing application to assign
to the moved ticket.

NewStatusID.description:
The ID of the status in the destination ticketing application to assign
to the moved ticket.

NewTicketTypeID.description:
The ID of the ticket type in the destination ticketing application to
assign to the moved ticket.

NewDayOff.description: A request to create one or more days off.

DateFrom.description: The date of the day off, or the start of the date range if creating multiple days.

DateTo.description:
The end of the date range. If omitted, only DateFrom is created.
Weekends and dates that are already days off will be skipped.
Cannot be more than 365 days after DateFrom.

Name.description: The name to apply to the created day(s) off.

NewProject.description: Represents a new project to be created.

AccountID.description: The ID of the account/department associated with the project.

AddContact.description: Whether new project members are automatically added as contacts. When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true (the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings. When inheritance is disabled, defaults to false. Value: true if new project members are automatically added as contacts; otherwise, false.

AlertOnAssignedHoursExceeded.description: Whether the project manager should be alerted periodically when assigned plan hours exceed assigned project hours. When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true (the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings. When inheritance is disabled, defaults to false. Value: true if the project manager will be alerted periodically when assigned plan hours exceed assigned project hours; otherwise, false.

AlertOnEstimatedHoursExceeded.description: Whether the project manager should be alerted periodically when estimated plan hours exceed estimated project hours. When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true (the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings. When inheritance is disabled, defaults to false. Value: true if the project manager will be alerted periodically when estimated plan hours exceed estimated project hours; otherwise, false.

AllocationEditMode.description:
The allocation edit mode which governs how resources are scheduled by resource pool managers from the Resource Management Console.
When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true
(the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings.
When inheritance is disabled and this is omitted, its value is 0, which does not
correspond to any named ResourceAllocationEditMode member — a value must be
explicitly supplied in that case.

AllowProjectTime.description: Whether the project allows project-level time entry. When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true (the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings. When inheritance is disabled, defaults to false. Value: true if the project allows project-level time entry; otherwise, false.

AlternateManagerUIDs.description: The UIDs of alternate managers for the project.

AppID.description: The project's application ID.

ApproveTimeByReportsTo.description: Whether project time is approved by the users who resources report to. When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true (the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings. When inheritance is disabled, defaults to false. Value: true if project time is approved by the "reports to" user for project resources; otherwise, false.

Attributes.description: The custom attributes associated with the project.

ClassificationID.description: The ID of the classification associated with the project.

EndDate.description: The end date of the project.

EstimatedHours.description: The estimated hours of the project.

ExpensesBudget.description: The expense budget of the project.

Health.description:
The health associated with the project. If a project health of 
On Hold, 
is specified, a project status with the status class of
On Hold must also be specified.

InheritProjectTypeSettings.description:
Whether or not to inherit project type settings to the newly created project.
This property defaults to true. When this value is set to true,
the following properties will be ignored:
AllowProjectTime
ApproveTimeByReportsTo
IsPublic
IsPublished
UpdateStartEnd
ScheduleHoursByPlan
UseRemainingHours
AlertOnEstimatedHoursExceeded
AlertOnAssignedHoursExceeded
AddContact
AllocationEditMode

IsActive.description: The active status of the project. Value: true if the project is active; otherwise, false.

IsPublic.description: The public status of the project. When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true (the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings. When inheritance is disabled, defaults to false. Value: true if the project is public; otherwise, false.

IsPublished.description: The published status of the project. When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true (the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings. When inheritance is disabled, defaults to false. Value: true if the project is published to authenticated users; otherwise, false.

ManagerUID.description: The UID of the user marked as the manager for the project.

Name.description: The name of the project.

PriorityID.description: The ID of the priority associated with the project.

ScheduleHoursByPlan.description: Whether resource allocation is managed by task assignments. When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true (the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings. When inheritance is disabled, defaults to false. Value: true if resource allocation is managed by task assignments; false when resources are allocated at the project-level regardless of task assignment.

ServiceID.description: The ID of the service associated with the project.

ServiceOfferingID.description: The ID of the service offering associated with the project.

SetProjectPctFromPlan.description: Whether the Project % Complete field on the project status update screen is pre-filled from the project's Plan Percent Complete value. When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true (the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings. When inheritance is disabled, defaults to false. Value: true to pre-fill from Plan Percent Complete; false to use the current Project % Complete.

SponsorUID.description: The UID of the user marked as the project's sponsor.

StartDate.description: The start date of the project.

StatusID.description:
The ID of the status associated with the project. Statuses with
classes of Cancelled or
Completed are invalid for creation. If
a status with a class of On Hold
is specified, the project health must also be set to On Hold.

TemplateID.description: The ID of the template to apply to the newly created project. Available templates to apply during creation follow the same restrictions as the web interface. The calling user must have access to the specified template either because they own it or it is a globally shared template. For service account callers, this means they may only specify globally shared templates since they cannot own a template themselves. When specifying to use a project template and choosing to inherit project type default settings, the project template will take precedence for any settings that overlap between itself and the project type default settings. Value: The ID of the template to apply to the newly created project. or 0 to not apply a template.

TimeBudget.description: The time budget of the project.

TypeID.description: The ID of the type associated with the project.

UpdateStartEnd.description: Whether the project's start date, end date, and estimated hours are updated based upon its associated plans. When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true (the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings. When inheritance is disabled, defaults to false. Value: true if the project's start date, end date, and estimated hours are updated based upon its associated plans; otherwise, false.

UseRemainingHours.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the project's tasks should be updated with remaining hours instead of percent complete. Whether task updates are managed by setting remaining hours or percent complete. When creating a project with InheritProjectTypeSettings set to true (the default), this value is ignored and inherited from the project type's settings. When inheritance is disabled, defaults to false. Value: true when tasks are updated using remaining hours, false when tasks are updated using percent complete.

NewUser.description: Represents a new user to be created in the system.

AboutMe.description: The "About Me" information associated with the new user.

AlertEmail.description:
The alert email address of the new user for receiving system notifications.

Remarks: When not provided, the primary email will be used.

AlternateEmail.description: The alternate email address of the new user.

AlternateID.description: The alternate ID of the new user.

Applications.description:
The system-defined (non-platform) applications
which should be granted to the new user.

ApplyTechnicianSignatureToReplies.description: Determines whether the technician signature associated with the new user is applied to the replies for all tickets and ticket tasks.

ApplyTechnicianSignatureToUpdatesAndComm.description: Determines whether the technician signature associated with the new user is applied to the updates and comments for all tickets and ticket tasks.

Attributes.description: The custom attributes associated with the new user.

AuthenticationProviderID.description:
The ID of the authentication provider the new user will use for authentication. Value: The ID of the authentication provider the new user will use for authentication, or null to use TeamDynamix or SSO authentication.

Remarks: This value can be obtained from the Admin application Authentication section by one of your organization's administrators who has access to modify authentication settings. If an invalid value is provided, the default authentication provider for the organization will be used. This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

AuthenticationUserName.description:
The authentication username of the new user, used for authenticating with non-TeamDynamix authentication types. Value: The user's authentication username.

Remarks: This value should be unique across all username and authentication usernames in your organization. If the provided value is not unique, it will be ignored. This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

Company.description: The company of the new user.

CostRate.description:
The cost rate of the new user.

Remarks: This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

DashboardID.description: The ID of the dashboard to assign to the new user.

DefaultAccountID.description: The ID of the default account/department associated with the new user.

DefaultAccountName.description: The name of the default account/department associated with the new user.

DefaultPriorityID.description: The ID of the default priority associated with the new user.

DefaultPriorityName.description: The name of the default priority associated with the new user.

DefaultRate.description:
The default bill rate of the new user.

Remarks: This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

DesktopID.description: The UID of the desktop to assign to the new user.

EndDate.description:
The date after which the new user is no longer available for scheduling and no longer required to log time.

Remarks: This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

ExternalID.description: The organizational ID of the new user.

Fax.description: The fax number of the new user.

FirstName.description: The first name of the new user.

GroupIDs.description:
The IDs of groups associated with the new user.

Remarks: This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

HomeAddress.description: The home address of the new user.

HomeCity.description: The home city of the new user.

HomeCountry.description: The home country of the new user.

HomePhone.description: The home phone number of the new user.

HomeState.description: The home state/province of the new user.

HomeZip.description: The home postal code of the new user.

IMHandle.description: The Instant Messenger (IM) username/handle associated with the new user.

IMProvider.description: The Instant Messenger (IM) provider associated with the new user.

IsActive.description: The active status of the new user. Ignored when creating a full user (TypeID = User) — those are always created active. Honored when creating Customers, Contacts, and service accounts, where omitting this creates an inactive record. Value: true if the user is active; otherwise, false.

IsCapacityManaged.description:
Whether the new user's capacity is managed, meaning they can have capacity and will appear on capacity/availability reports. Value: true if this user's capacity is managed; otherwise, false.

Remarks: This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

IsConfidential.description:
The confidential status of the new user. Value: true if the new user is confidential; otherwise, false.

Remarks: Confidential users cannot be seen by unprivileged individuals within a client portal application.

IsEmployee.description:
The employee status of the new user. Value: true if the new user is an employee; otherwise, false.

Remarks: This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

LastName.description: The last name of the new user.

LinkDashboard.description: Whether or not to link the dashboard to the template.

LinkDesktop.description: Whether or not to link the desktop to the template.

LocationID.description: The ID of the location associated with the user.

LocationRoomID.description: The ID of the location room associated with the user.

LongDateFormatID.description:
The ID of the long-date format associated with the new user. Supply `0` to inherit the
organization's format; defaults to `0` when omitted.
            
Valid values:
            
- `0` = Use organization format
- `1` = `ddd M/d/yyyy` (e.g. Tue 4/7/2026)
- `2` = `ddd d/M/yyyy` (e.g. Tue 7/4/2026)
- `3` = `ddd yyyy-MM-dd` (e.g. Tue 2026-04-07)
- `4` = `ddd d-MMM-yyyy` (e.g. Tue 7-Apr-2026)
- `5` = `ddd M/d/yy` (e.g. Tue 4/7/26)
- `6` = `ddd d/M/yy` (e.g. Tue 7/4/26)
- `7` = `ddd d-MMM-yy` (e.g. Tue 7-Apr-26)

LongDateFormatLabel.description: The display label (format pattern) of the long-date format associated with the new user.

MiddleName.description: The middle name of the new user.

MobilePhone.description: The mobile phone number of the new user.

Nickname.description: The nickname of the new user.

OrgApplications.description:
The organizationally-defined (platform) applications for this user.

Remarks: This only applies to Users after creation and will be ignored for Customers.

OtherPhone.description: The other phone number of the new user.

Pager.description: The pager number of the new user.

Password.description: The password of the new user.

Permissions.description:
The global security role permissions for the new user.

Remarks: Each value refers to the ID of a permission. This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

PrimaryClientPortalApplicationID.description:
The ID of the primary client portal application for the new user. Value: The ID of the primary client portal application for the new user, or null to use the organization default.

Remarks: Leave this value blank to use the organization default as the primary client portal application for this user. This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

PrimaryEmail.description: The primary email address of the new user.

PrimaryPhone.description:
The primary phone number of the new user.

Remarks: Recognized values are:

  • Work
  • Home
  • Pager
  • Mobile
  • Other
  • Fax

Values outside of this set are equivalent to specifying the work phone.

ReferenceID.description:
The integer ID of the new user.

Remarks: This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

ReportsToFullName.description: The full name of the user who the new user reports to.

ReportsToUID.description: The UID of the user who the new user reports to.

ReportTimeAfterDate.description:
The date after which the new user should start reporting time. This also governs capacity calculations.

Remarks: This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

ResourcePoolID.description:
The ID of the resource pool associated with the new user.

Remarks: This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

ResourcePoolName.description: The name of the resource pool associated with the new user.

Salutation.description: The salutation of the new user.

SecurityRoleID.description:
The UID of the global security role associated with the new user.

Remarks: This is required when creating Users, and is ignored when creating Customers.

SecurityRoleName.description: The name of the global security role associated with the new user.

ShortDateFormatID.description:
The ID of the short-date format associated with the new user. Supply `0` to inherit the
organization's format; defaults to `0` when omitted.
            
Valid values:
            
- `0` = Use organization format
- `1` = `M/d/yyyy` (e.g. 4/7/2026)
- `2` = `d/M/yyyy` (e.g. 7/4/2026)
- `3` = `yyyy-MM-dd` (e.g. 2026-04-07)
- `4` = `d-MMM-yyyy` (e.g. 7-Apr-2026)

ShortDateFormatLabel.description: The display label (format pattern) of the short-date format associated with the new user.

ShouldReportTime.description:
Whether the new user should report time. Value: true if the new user should report time; otherwise, false.

Remarks: This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

TechnicianSignature.description: The technician signature associated with the new user.

TimeFormatID.description:
The ID of the time format associated with the new user. Supply `0` to inherit the organization's
format; defaults to `0` when omitted.
            
Valid values:
            
- `0` = Use organization format
- `1` = `h:mm tt` (e.g. 8:02 PM)
- `2` = `HH:mm` (e.g. 20:02)

TimeFormatLabel.description: The display label (format pattern) of the time format associated with the new user.

Title.description: The title of the new user.

TypeID.description: The type of the new user.

TZID.description: The ID of the time zone associated with the new user. Value: The ID of the time zone associated with the new user, or 0 to use the time zone specified for the organization.

TZName.description: The name of the time zone associated with the new user.

UserName.description:
The username of the new user, for use when using TeamDynamix authentication.

Remarks: This is required when creating users, but is not required when creating customers.

WorkableHours.description:
The number of workable hours in a work day for the new user.

Remarks: This only applies to Users and will be ignored when creating Customers.

WorkAddress.description: The work address of the new user.

WorkCity.description: The work city of the new user.

WorkCountry.description: The work country of the new user.

WorkPhone.description: The work phone number of the new user.

WorkState.description: The work state/province of the new user.

WorkZip.description: The work postal code of the new user.

ProjectCloseRequest.description: Encapsulates the parameters required to close a project via the API.

CloseIssues.description:
Whether to close all open issues on the project.
When true, NewIssueStatusID must be provided.

CloseRisks.description:
Whether to close all open risks on the project.
When true, NewRiskStatusID must be provided.

CloseTasks.description: Whether to close all open tasks on the project.

Health.description: The health rating for the project at closure.

IsActive.description: Whether the project should remain active (visible) after closure.

NewIssueStatusID.description:
The status ID to assign to open issues when CloseIssues is true.
Must be an active issue status for the project's application with a Completed or Cancelled status class.

NewRiskStatusID.description:
The status ID to assign to open risks when CloseRisks is true.
Must be an active risk status for the project's application with a Completed or Cancelled status class.

PercentComplete.description: The percent complete to record on the project at closure. Defaults to 100.

StatusID.description:
The ID of the closure status to assign to the project.
Must be an active, closure-type project status for the project's application.

StatusText.description: A free-text status message to record on the project at closure.

SurveyID.description: The ID of the survey to send at closure, if any.

SurveyRecipients.description: The classes of project members who should receive the closure survey.

SurveyRecipientUIDs.description: Additional individual user UIDs to include as survey recipients.

allOf.description: A feed entry to be submitted to a project.

Health.description:
The new health for the project. When supplied, triggers a status-update entry. Must be a
non-None HealthChoice (Green=1, Yellow=2, Red=3, OnHold=4). When omitted,
the project's current health is retained.

NewStatusID.description:
The new status ID for the project. When supplied and greater than zero, triggers
a status-update entry. When omitted or zero, the project's current status is retained.

NewPercentComplete.description:
The new percent complete for the project (0–100). When supplied, triggers a
status-update entry. When omitted, the project's current percent complete is retained.

ProjectManagerUpdate.description: A request to change the managers (primary and alternate) on a project.

AlternateManagerUIDs.description:
The UIDs of the alternate managers to apply. Omit (or send null) to leave the project's
alternate managers unchanged. See ReplaceExistingAlternateManagers for whether the
supplied UIDs are added to the existing alternate managers or replace the whole set.

ManagerUID.description:
The UID of the user to set as the project's primary manager. Omit (or send null) to
leave the current primary manager unchanged. An empty GUID is rejected — a project must always
have a primary manager.

ReplaceExistingAlternateManagers.description:
How AlternateManagerUIDs is applied. When false (the default), the supplied
UIDs are added to the project's existing alternate managers. When true, they replace the
entire set — an empty list clears all alternate managers. Ignored when
AlternateManagerUIDs is null.

ReportPromptInfo.description:
Describes a prompted filter on a report - that is, a filter whose
value is supplied at run time rather than fixed on the report definition.

ColumnID.description: The ID of the column the prompt filters on. Value: The ID of the column the prompt filters on. May optionally be supplied as ColumnID as a cross-check when supplying a value for this prompt via Number.

DataType.description: The data type of the value expected by the prompt.

IsRequired.description: A value indicating whether the prompt requires a value to be supplied. Value: true if a value is always required for this prompt; otherwise, false.

Name.description: The display name of the prompt.

Number.description: The number identifying this prompt's filter within the report. Value: The number identifying this prompt's filter within the report. This number is unique within the report, but it is neither contiguous nor stable across edits to the report's filters - callers should re-fetch the report rather than persisting it. Use this value as the Number when supplying a value for this prompt.

Operator.description: The operator this prompt's filter applies. Value: The operator this prompt's filter applies, such as >=. Two prompts on the same column - the two ends of a date range, for example - share a Name and differ only by Operator.

ReportPromptValue.description: A value to apply to one of a report's prompted filters.

ColumnID.description: The ID of the column whose prompt this value applies to. Value: An optional cross-check for the ID of the column whose prompt this value applies to. When supplied and it does not match the prompt's actual column, the request is rejected. Corresponds to ColumnID as returned by the report's prompt metadata.

Number.description: The number identifying the prompt's filter that this value applies to. Value: The number identifying the prompt's filter that this value applies to. Corresponds to Number as returned by the report's prompt metadata.

Value.description:
The value to filter on for the prompt. For a prompt whose operator takes no arguments, the
value selects the operator instead - only "true" or "false" are accepted, and no value
leaves the prompt unchanged.

Value: The value to filter on for the prompt. Providing an empty string (or omitting this property) clears the prompt's filter criteria - non-required prompts with no value will not filter on that dimension, while required prompts with no value will result in a validation error. A prompt whose operator takes no arguments has no criteria to clear - no value leaves it unchanged.

when a ticket reaches a certain percentage of its respond-by or resolve-by deadline.

The percentage of the SLA deadline at which this step fires,
expressed as an integer from 1 to 10000 (where 100 = 100% of the deadline).
Values above 100 represent time after the deadline has passed.

The ID of the group to reassign the ticket to when this step fires.

Valid values can be retrieved from POST /api/groups/search.

Represents an error that occurred trying to perform an operation (typically a bulk operation)
in a time and expenses API operation. See the ErrorMessage and ErrorCode for more details as
well as the TimeEntryID and Index for more information on which operation failed.

TimeEntryID.description: The ID of the time entry associated with the error.

TimeApiErrorCode.description:
A list of error codes to help the user understand item errors for time API operations.

| Name | Value | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| Unknown | 0 | Represents an unknown / unexpected error |
| Server Error | 1 | An exception occurred on the server while processing the request and prevented the request from completing properly. |
| Invalid Time Entry ID | 10 | The time entry identifier was either not specified when it was required or was an unsupported value. See the error message for more details. |
| Invalid Module Type | 11 | Occurs when you attempt to change a time entry's component after it already exists or to a component that does not support time entry. |
| Invalid Project ID | 12 | Occurs when a project ID is required but not specified or specified to a negative value. |
| Invalid Plan ID | 13 | Occurs when a plan ID is required but not specified or specified to a negative value. |
| Invalid Item ID | 14 | Occurs when an item ID is required but not specified or specified to a negative value. |
| Invalid App ID | 15 | Occurs when an application ID is required but not specified or specified to a negative value. |
| User Not Found | 20 | Occurs when no user with the specified unique identifier could be found. They either do not exist, are deactivated, or are not visible to the user executing the request. |
| Time Entry Not Found | 21 | Occurs when trying to act on a time entry that already exists but either is deleted, has an incorrect ID specified, or is not visible to the executing user. |
| Time Account Not Found | 22 | Occurs when trying to add time to an item when the specified time account is not available for that item. |
| Task Not Found | 23 | Occurs when trying to work with time on a Task that either is deleted, has an incorrect ID specified, or is not visible to the executing user. |
| Issue Not Found | 24 | Occurs when trying to work with time on an Issue that either is deleted, has an incorrect ID specified, or is not visible to the executing user. |
| Ticket Not Found | 25 | Occurs when trying to work with time on a Ticket that either is deleted, has an incorrect ID specified, or is not visible to the executing user. |
| Ticket Task Not Found | 26 | Occurs when trying to work with time on a Ticket Task that either is deleted, has an incorrect ID specified, or is not visible to the executing user. |
| Ticket Converted To Task | 27 | Occurs when trying to work with time on a Ticket that has already been converted to a Task. You should enter time against the task instead. |
| Project Not Found | 28 | Occurs when trying to work with time on a Project, Issue, or Task where the related project has been deleted. |
| User Does Not Have Application | 30 | Occurs when the user the time entry belongs to does not have the Time and Expenses application or the application that contains the item they're trying to add time to. |
| User Is Not On Project | 31 | Occurs when a user the time entry will be for is not an approved member of the project. |
| Cannot Add Time For Others | 32 | Occurs when you are trying to add time for another user but you do not have the permission to add time for other users. |
| Cannot View Time Entry | 33 | Occurs when you are trying to view time that you do not have permissions to view. |
| User Invalid | 34 | Occurs when the user the time entry belongs to is not active or is not a standard user. |
| Time Report Already Approved | 40 | The time report the entry would belong to has already been approved. |
| Time Report Already Submitted | 41 | The time report the entry would belong to has already been submitted. |
| Time Entry Occurs On Locked Date | 42 | The time entry occurs on a date that is locked. |
| Time Account Limit Exceeded | 43 | The time account is limited and the edit or addition would move the user over their limit for a specific period of time. |
| Limited Time Cannot Be Negative | 44 | Occurs when a user edits or adds a time entry on a limited time type that would make the time entry negative. |
| Cannot Change Property | 50 | Occurs when the value of a property that cannot be edited is modified. If you need to change this value, you should instead delete the time entry and add a new time entry. |
| Max Operations Per Request Exceeded | 51 | Occurs when too many operations are included in a single bulk operation. |
| No Operations Specified | 52 | Occurs when a bulk operation occurred but no operations were specified. |
| Project Not Active | 53 | Occurs when trying to work with time on a project, issue, or task when the project is no longer active. |
| Project Time Entry Not Allowed | 54 | Occurs when trying to enter time at the project level but the project does not support project-level time entry. |
| Limited Time Types Unavailable | 55 | Occurs when trying to work with limited time types on components that don't support them. |
| Cannot Delete Time Entry | 56 | Occurs when trying to delete a time entry for another user. |
| Invalid Time Date | 57 | Occurs when required timedate is not provided. |
| Invalid Ticket ID | 58 | Occurs when a ticket ID is required but not specified or specified to a negative value. |
| Portfolio Not Found | 59 | Occurs when trying to work with time on a Portfolio, Portfolio Issue where the related portfolio has been deleted. |
| Portfolio Not Active | 60 | Occurs when trying to work with time on a Portfolio, Portfolio Issue where the related portfolio is no longer active. |
